notes.4.38: 'uureſt' (line 4.82) is obscure; the line seems to want 'that you never die a sudden death', and a negative may have been lost. Simêdio and Sirages are probably Media and Rages of the Book of Tobit. Lines 4.71-4.72 (Mary) stand without a verb.

nodes.text: May the holy five wounds bless you
on either side, there beside [you];
may the heavenly warrior stand by you.
Go in God's peace;
may the holy angel protect you.
May your heart be of stone,
may your body be of bone,
may your head be of steel,
may heaven be a shield to you.
May hell be barred before you;
may all evil go astray before you;
may paradise be open to you;
may all weapons be locked before you,
so that they utterly refrain
from any of them stabbing or cutting you.
The moon and the sun too,
may they shine for you with delight.
May the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit
let you live in well-being.
The twelve apostles,
may they honour you before God,
so that your lords may be glad to see you.
May every good thing befall you.
The good St Stephen,
who overcame all his distress,
may he stand by you
wherever you have need and want of him.
St John
and the four evangelists,
may they counsel you for the best.
My lady St Mary,
the noble and free,
with much of holy Christ's blood
may you be hallowed, so that your soul
be not thrust out of the kingdom of heaven, nor out of worldly honours.
May God bless you still more.
May St Gall look after your food;
may St Gertrude give you good lodging.
May your life be blessed;
may men and women be kind to you.
May good counsel be yours,
that you ever die a *uureſt* death.
So the good St Tobias blessed his son, and then sent him
into a land, to a city called Simêdio;
the stronghold was called Sirages.
